purpose: What each wage source's own headline figure actually contains — the audit that makes package 9's normalisation rule enforceable ('subtract a component the source publishes separately; never add one the source never measured'). Curated, evidenced data — like data/occupations.json, not derived from a live API. Every field is true/false/"unknown" WITH a citation; "unknown" is a genuine unchecked gap, not a soft no.

authoritative_frameworks.eurostat_ses_b411: Structure of Earnings Survey variable B411 — 'annual bonuses and allowances not paid at each pay period'. Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1526, which replaced Reg. 530/1999. The EU's own reference definition for what this file calls irregular_bonus.
authoritative_frameworks.eurostat_lcs_categories: Labour Cost Survey: D.11112 (irregular bonuses/allowances) vs D.11111 (direct pay for time worked) vs D.12 (employers' social security contributions, incl. pension). This file's employer_social_contributions maps to D.12; irregular_bonus to D.11112.
authoritative_frameworks.ilo_12th_icls_1973_para10: The 12th International Conference of Labour Statisticians (1973), paragraph 10, resolution on wage statistics — the base international definition every national office's own concept ultimately traces back to, cited here as the common ancestor, not because any single national source follows it verbatim.
authoritative_frameworks.eurostat_own_caveat: Eurostat's own published sentence on why a naive x12 of a monthly figure understates annual pay: "Annual earnings hence usually exceed the figure produced by multiplying the 'standard monthly package' by 12." — the reason this whole audit exists, in the standard-setter's own words.

field_definitions.irregular_bonus: 13th/14th month, Christmas bonus, holiday bonus, profit share — true/false/unknown, matches Eurostat B411/D.11112 in spirit though not every national concept maps to it exactly.
field_definitions.overtime: Whether the headline figure includes overtime pay.
field_definitions.employer_social_contributions: Employer-paid pension, ATP, superannuation or equivalent — matches LCS D.12. This is the component this pipeline's normalise.py may SUBTRACT (never add) when a source publishes it separately.
field_definitions.gross_or_net: Whether the headline figure is gross or net of income tax/employee social contributions.
field_definitions.concept_name: The office's own term for its headline figure, in its own language, verbatim.
field_definitions.separately_published_components: Which of the above the source ALSO publishes as its own distinct figure — i.e. what can honestly be subtracted, sourced, rather than estimated.

sources.note: SCB's own wage-structure-statistics documentation: "en 13:e eller 14:e manadslon samt vinstdelning ... ingar inte i lonestatistiken" (a 13th or 14th month salary and profit-sharing are not included in the wage statistics) — carried from this package's work order, not independently re-fetched from SCB's PDF methodology this session (the API's own JSON-stat response carries no prose methodology text to check against). x12 is therefore a floor, not the true annual figure — Eurostat's own caveat applies directly.

sources.note: BLS's own OEWS methodology explicitly distinguishes production bonuses/incentive pay (in scope) from non-production bonuses like year-end discretionary bonuses (out of scope) — this asymmetry is why OEWS reads low against ES/UK/DK/AU's annual, bonus-inclusive measures even before any FX/period conversion. Carried from the work order; BLS's own OEWS methodology page is the citation, not re-fetched this session.

sources.note: INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED LIVE this package (Tier 1): DST's LONS20 table publishes PENS ('Pension including ATP in DKK per hour worked') and UREGEL ('Irregular payments...') as real, separately-queryable components of the same cross-tabulated cell as FORINKL. 2512/2024: FORINKL=489.26, BASIS=403.50, PENS=59.35, UREGEL=9.06 DKK/hour — consistent with PENS and UREGEL being components that sum toward FORINKL's total (403.50+59.35+9.06=471.91, the residual ~17 DKK/hr plausibly covered by smaller unfetched components: overtime, sick pay, nuisance bonus, fringe benefits, holiday allowances). This is the ONE source in this file where the header figure's own PENS component was independently confirmed live, not carried from the work order's table unverified — see scripts/src_salary_dk.py.

Månedslønn = avtalt lønn (agreed pay) + uregelmessige tillegg (irregular allowances) + bonus, per SSB's own definition — bonus is IN by construction, unlike Sweden/Finland. feriepenger (holiday pay, statutory 10.2%) is explicitly excluded, since it is a separate annual payment that effectively REPLACES the June salary rather than adding to it (net annual effect ~+1.1-1.4%, not the full 10.2%, per Ferieloven §10's mechanics) — carried from the work order, not independently re-verified against SSB's own methodology PDF this session.

sources.note: INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED LIVE this package (Tier 1): table StatFin/pra/15au publishes koko_psaaja_kans_* (total_*, includes overtime) and koko_psaaja_sans_* (regular_*, excludes it) as two parallel, separately-queryable content-code families — Finland needs no subtraction to get a 'regular pay' figure, unlike Denmark. 2512/2024 private sector: total_mean=5316, regular_mean=5253 EUR/month (regular < total, consistent with overtime being excluded from regular_*). No 13th/14th month or profit share in either basis, per Tilastokeskus's own wage-concept documentation carried from the work order.

Spain's ganancia anual already includes the two statutory pagas extraordinarias (Christmas and summer bonuses, ET art.31) INSIDE the headline figure — this pipeline must never add a '13th/14th month' uplift to Spain, since it is already counted. Carried from the work order's own research; INE's EES methodology note is the citation, not independently re-fetched this session beyond the vintage/table-identity checks already done in package 8/Tier 1.

CBS's bruto uurloon explicitly EXCLUDES bijzondere beloningen (special remuneration: vakantiegeld/holiday allowance >=8% statutory per WML art.15, 13th month, profit shares) — the Dutch figure in this spine understates total compensation by roughly that margin, disclosed here rather than corrected for (this pipeline does not synthesise the missing ~16% from a statutory minimum, since actual collectively-agreed vakantiegeld/13th-month provision varies by employer and is not itself published per-occupation). Carried from the work order's research; CBS's own StatLine table documentation is the citation.

pay_cycle_context._note: Background explaining WHY sources differ — sourced, but deliberately kept separate from the composition fields above and from any calculation. Never used to derive a number; used only to explain one.
pay_cycle_context.NL: Vakantiebijslag: statutory minimum 8% of annual pay (Wet minimumloon en minimumvakantiebijslag, WML art.15).
pay_cycle_context.ES: Two statutory pagas extraordinarias (Christmas and summer bonuses), Estatuto de los Trabajadores art.31 — already inside ganancia anual, see salary_es entry above.
pay_cycle_context.DK: Ferietillæg: 1% for salaried employees, 12.5% for hourly-paid, per Ferieloven §16.
pay_cycle_context.NO: Feriepenger: 10.2% statutory (Ferieloven §10), but the net annual effect is smaller (~1.1-1.4%) because it functionally replaces June's regular salary rather than adding to it in full.
pay_cycle_context.FI: Lomaraha: approximately 4-6%, collectively agreed, not a statutory entitlement.
pay_cycle_context.DE: Weihnachtsgeld (Christmas bonus): paid to roughly 51% of employees per available survey data, governed by collective bargaining agreements (CBAs), not statute.
pay_cycle_context.AU: Superannuation: 12% employer contribution since 1 Jul 2025 (Superannuation Guarantee (Administration) Act 1992, s.19(2)) — on top of, not inside, salary-or-wages.
pay_cycle_context.IT: Tredicesima (13th month) and, per some CCNLs, quattordicesima (14th month) — collectively agreed. No occupation-level Italian wage source exists in this pipeline to apply this context to (see src_salary_it.py) — retained here for completeness of the region's pay-cycle picture.
pay_cycle_context.AE_QA: End-of-service gratuity is a severance entitlement under UAE/Qatar labour law, paid on termination — NOT an ongoing pay component, and explicitly out of scope for this file's fields.
